correctness.rationale: A shortest path between two vertices on a single cycle fiber cannot spend any steps changing rows. Four chosen points on one cycle fiber block both arcs for an alternating pair, proving the known upper bound 3s. With n=3q+u the gaps of the given starts are (q,q,q), (q,q,q+1), or (q,q+1,q+1). The short-arc condition is q>=2s-2 for u=0,2 and q>=2s-1 for u=1; these hold throughout the stated domain including n=6s-6, and imply q>=s+1. Each band has s columns and is separated from its cyclic successor by at least one empty column. For a same-band pair the horizontal-then-vertical route uses a shortest arc and hits the terminal band column only in its selected row. Any two different bands can be oriented as cyclic successors. The forward distance h_j+t-r is positive and at most n/2, and the entire vertical leg can be put in the first unused column past the initial band; the row legs meet only the chosen endpoints. This works also with equal rows and tied shortest cyclic arcs. Thus all 3s vertices are mutually visible without a finite-to-infinite inference.
residual_risks: The result explicitly excludes n=6s-5 and other shorter uncovered circumferences. The bounded BFS is illustrative; correctness for the entire domain rests on the explicit geodesic construction.
